questions.question: If two cars travel the exact same distance, how does the speed of the faster car affect its travel time compared to the slower car?
options: The faster car takes more time.
The faster car takes a shorter time.
The faster car takes the same amount of time.
The faster car's time depends on its weight.

questions.question: Which formula is used to calculate the speed of an object?
options: Speed = distance x time
Speed = time / distance
Speed = distance / time
Speed = distance + time

questions.question: What is the effect of a resultant force acting on a moving object?
options: It can change the speed of the object.
It always keeps the object at a constant speed.
It has no effect on the object's speed.
It instantly reduces the object's mass to zero.

questions.question: On a distance-time graph, what does a steeper line with a greater gradient represent?
options: The object is moving slower.
The object is stationary.
The object is moving faster.
The object is moving backwards only.

questions.question: When does a falling object reach its terminal velocity?
options: When gravity becomes zero.
When the drag force is greater than gravity.
When the drag and gravitational forces are equal.
When it first starts to fall.

questions.question: How does increasing the surface area of a parachute affect its drag force?
options: It makes the drag force bigger.
It makes the drag force smaller.
It has no effect on the drag force.
It reduces the gravity acting on it.

questions.question: When a skydiver with a parachute is falling at top speed, how does the force of drag compare to the force of gravity on the jumper?
options: Drag is much smaller than gravity.
Drag is the same size as gravity.
Drag is twice as large as gravity.
Drag is zero.

questions.question: What does a horizontal, level line on a distance-time graph represent?
options: The object is moving at a steady high speed.
The object is accelerating.
The object is stationary with no movement.
The object is moving backwards.

questions.question: On a distance-time graph, what is indicated by upward sloping lines compared to downward sloping lines?
options: Movement in opposite directions.
Movement at the exact same constant speed only.
That the object is stationary in both cases.
That the object is gaining mass.

questions.question: What is meant by the instantaneous speed of an object?
options: The speed of the object over an entire journey.
The speed of the object at a particular moment in time.
The maximum speed the object can possibly reach.
The speed of an object when it is at rest.

questions.question: Why is it beneficial to take repeat readings during an experiment?
options: To make the experiment take longer.
To reduce the effect of random errors.
To eliminate systematic errors completely.
To guarantee that all readings are anomalous.

questions.question: What should you do with anomalous readings when calculating average values?
options: Include them normally in the calculation.
Double their value before adding them.
Exclude them so they are not used in calculations of averages.
Replace all other readings with the anomalous reading.

questions.question: In which direction does friction act on a moving object?
options: In the same direction as the movement.
Against the direction of movement of the object.
Upwards, perpendicular to the movement.
Downwards, in the direction of gravity.

questions.question: If no resultant force is acting on a moving object, what will happen to its motion?
options: It will slowly come to a stop.
It will continue to move at a steady speed in a straight line.
It will instantly speed up.
It will begin to move in a circle.

questions.question: What is the primary physical effect of streamlining an object?
options: It increases the gravitational pull on the object.
It reduces the drag force on the object.
It increases the mass of the object.
It makes the object stationary.

questions.question: How does the speed of an object moving through a fluid affect the drag force acting on it?
options: The drag force increases with speed.
The drag force decreases as speed increases.
The drag force remains completely constant at all speeds.
The drag force immediately drops to zero once the object moves.
